title: OLE2 next-opportunity survey: a source-backed XLS open is now CPU, and most of it decodes strings nobody asked for
code_state: no file under crates/ was modified by this batch
reason_codes: the highest-ranked opportunity changes when a malformed UTF-16 shared string is refused, which is a tested contract and needs a frozen design record first
the second-ranked opportunity raises read counts on the majority of the corpus and needs a density gate designed with it
the third-ranked opportunity changes which CFB primitive the globals scan uses and would have to prove read and observation counts unchanged
no before/after pair and no A/B/B/A matrix were captured, so no speedup is admissible from this batch

accepted_evidence.deterministic_counters: nine cells, three source implementations by three operations, 20 warmups and 100 samples, every logical counter constant across all samples; reproduces change 0565's retained read and byte counts exactly as a control
accepted_evidence.hardware_counters: perf stat isolation pairs at 1100 and 100 samples divided by 1000
accepted_evidence.instruction_attribution: callgrind isolation pairs on three fixtures of different globals composition, self and inclusive
accepted_evidence.static_model: consumed-closure and composition models over 126 XLS fixtures, olefile plus the standard library, no repository code executed
accepted_evidence.corpus_regression: one open of each of the 117 XLS fixtures that open, fitted to three byte classes, R^2 0.9933

accepted_costs.latency_scope: single-leg attribution medians only; warm page cache, staged immutable copy, one host, one binary
accepted_costs.callgrind_string_ops: memset and memcpy instruction counts are upper bounds because Valgrind instruments ERMS string loops per iteration

known_gaps.formats: no DOC or PPT scenario was measured; only the CFB findings transfer without fresh measurement
known_gaps.concentration: both leading opportunities are concentrated: 90% of skippable globals bytes live in 15 of 126 fixtures, and only 7 of 117 fixtures have an SST above a quarter of their globals
known_gaps.regression_separability: the SST and other-closure coefficients are within 6% of each other and their classes correlate with globals size, so the regression establishes that consumed bytes dominate, not the SST share specifically
known_gaps.change_0547: its absolute instruction magnitudes cannot be bound to this tree because its fixture and harness binding is not reproducible from the retained record
known_gaps.fixtures: 9 of 126 XLS fixtures do not open, including all three encrypted ones, and are excluded rather than imputed

withheld: any speedup, cold-cache, physical-device, remote or range-source, peak-RSS, allocation-profile, concurrency-scaling, real-producer or cross-platform result

provenance.note: a candidate implementing opportunity 1 entered the working tree after every capture in this packet; this packet is its before leg and measures none of it
